Facility Patient Conference Fee - Per 15 minutes or major portion thereof When requested by a facility to review ongoing management of the patient in that facility or to determine whether a patient with complex supportive care needs in a facility can safely return to the community or transition to a supportive or long-term facility. Must be performed in a facility and results of the conference must be recorded in the patient chart. Facilities limited to: hospital, palliative care facility, LTC facility, detox/drug and alcohol facility. Requires interdisciplinary team meeting of at least 2 allied care professionals in total, and will include family members when available. Fee includes: Where appropriate, interviewing of and conferencing with patient, family members, and other allied care providers of both the acute care facility and community. Review and organization of appropriate clinical information.¿ The integration of relevant information into the formulation of an action plan for the clinical care of the patient upon discharge from the acute care facility, including provision of degrees of intervention and end of life documentation as appropriate. The care plan must be recorded and must include patient identifiers, reason for the care plan, list of co-morbidities, safety risks, list of interventions, what referrals to be made, what follow-up has been arranged. Maximum payable per patient is 90 minutes (6 units) per fiscal year. Maximum payable on any one day is 30 minutes (2 units). Start and end times of the service must be documented both on the claim submission and the patient's chart. Not payable to physicians who are employed by or who are under contract to a facility who would otherwise have attended the conference as a requirement of their employment or contract with the facility; or physicians working under salary, service contract or sessional arrangements. Visit payable in addition if medically required and does not take place concurrently with the patient conference.

Community Patient Conference Fee - Per 15 Minutes or major portion thereof Creation of a coordinated clinical action plan for the care of community-based patients with more complex needs. Payable only when coordination of care and two way collaborative conferencing with other allied care providers is required (e.g., psychologists or counsellors, long-term workers, home care or specialty care nurses, physiotherapists, occupational ¿therapists, social workers), as well as with the patient and will include family¿ members when available (as required due to the severity of the patient's condition). Fee includes: The interviewing of patient and family members as indicated and the conferencing with other allied care providers. Review and organization of appropriate clinical information. The integration of relevant information into the formulation of an action plan for the clinical care of the patient. The care plan must be recorded in the patient's chart and must include patient identifiers, reason for the care plan, list of co-morbidities, safety risks, list of interventions, what referrals to be made, what follow-up has been arranged. Maximum payable per patient is 90 minutes (6 units) per fiscal year. Maximum payable on any one day is 30 minutes (2 units). Claim must state start and end times of service. Start and end times must be documented in the patient chart. Not payable to physicians who are employed by, or who are under contract to a facility, who would otherwise have attended the conference as a requirement of their employment or contract with the facility; or physicians working under salary, service contract or sessional arrangements. Visit payable in addition if medically required and does not take place concurrently with clinical action plan.

Multidisciplinary Conferencing for Complex Patients - Per 15 minutes or major portion thereof A scheduled session/meeting to discuss and plan medical management of patients with serious and complex problems. Payable only when coordination of care is required via a collaborative conference with at least two of the following: other specialists, GPs, allied health providers and/or coordinators of the patient's care. Includes scheduled face to face, telephone or video technology communication regarding assessment, clinical coordination and management of a complex patient. Patient must have one of the following: Multiple medical needs or complex co-morbidities where care needs to be coordinated over a period of time between several health disciplines, and provide the appropriate ICD Code(s) Diagnosis of malignancy (excluding non-melanoma skin cancer). One morbidity plus a minimum of one of the following non-medical conditions: poor socioeconomic status, unstable home environment, dependency on family/caregiver for daily living tasks, accessibility/mobility issues, under care of Child Protection Unit, received Tertiary or Acute level of care related to psychiatric condition within the previous 6 Months, frail elderly, >75 years old, BMI >35 or high readmission rate. All physicians involved in the conference may each independently bill for this fee. Each physician involved in the case conference must document their contribution to the discussion and its effect on the patient’s overall care in the medical record/chart along with the start and end times of the conference, and the names and job titles of the other participants at the meeting. Claim must state start and end times for the service. Maximum of 4 units may be claimed per patient per physician per day. Maximum of 16 units per patient per physician per fiscal year.

General Practice Acute Care Discharge Conference fee - per 15 minutes or portion thereof. This fee is billable when a Discharge Planning Conference is performed regarding a patient with complex supportive care needs, for review of condition(s) and planning for safe discharge. Payable only for patients being discharged from an acute care facility to the community or to a different facility; another acute care facility, or a supportive care or Long Term Care facility. Must be performed in the acute care facility and results of the conference must be recorded in the patient’s chart in the acute care facility. Face-to-face conferencing is required. Requires interdisciplinary team meeting of the GP assuming MRP status upon discharge and a minimum of 2 other allied care professionals, and will include family members when appropriate. Fee includes: Where appropriate, interviewing of and conferencing with patient, family members, and other allied care providers of both the acute care facility and community. Review and organization of appropriate clinical information. The integration of relevant information into the formulation of an action plan for the clinical care of the patient upon discharge from the acute care facility, including provision of degrees of intervention and end of life documentation as appropriate. The care plan must be recorded in patient chart and must include patient identifiers, reason for the care plan, list of co-morbidities, safety risks, list of interventions, what referrals to be made, what follow-up has been arranged. This fee does not cover routine discharge planning from an acute-care facility, nor is this fee payable for conferencing with acute-care nurses during the course of a patient’s stay in the acute care facility. Maximum payable per patient is 90 minutes (6 units) per fiscal year. Maximum payable on any one day is 30 minutes (2 units). Claim must state start and end times of the service. Not payable to physicians who are employed by or who are under contract to a facility who would otherwise have attended the conference as a requirement of their employment or contract with the facility; or physicians working under salary, service contract or sessional arrangements.

Urgent Telephone Conference with a Specialist - Limit of 3 calls per patient per physician per day. Conferencing on an urgent basis (within 8 hours) with a specialist or GP with specialty training by telephone, including documentation, and implementation of a clinical action plan for the care of patients with acute needs. Payable to the GP or Specialist who initiates a two-way telephone communication with another specialist or GP with specialty training regarding the urgent assessment and management of a patient but without the responding physician seeing the patient. The care plan must be recorded in the patient chart and must include patient identifiers, reason for the care plan, list of comorbidities, safety risks, list of interventions, what referrals to be made, what follow-up has been arranged. Not payable to physicians who are employed by, or who are under a contract to a facility, who would otherwise have provided the service as a requirement of their employment or contract with the facility; or physicians working under salary, service contract or sessional arrangement. Include start time in time fields when submitting claim. Out-of-Office Hours Premiums may not be claimed in addition. Visit payable on same date of service if medically required. NOTE: Not payable for situations where the primary purpose of the call is to: i) Book an appointment ii) Arrange for transfer of care that occurs within 24 hours iii) Arrange for an expedited consultation or procedure within 24 hours iv) Arrange for laboratory or diagnostic investigations v) Inform the other physician of results of diagnostic investigations vi) Arrange a hospital bed for the patient vii) Obtain non-urgent advice for patient management (i.e. not required within the next 24 hours).

GP Prescription renewal phone call, fax, email - Payment is restricted to prescription renewals initiated by a pharmacist. This service is not to be used as routine practice or to authorize repeat prescriptions for which long term repeats would more properly authorized at the time of writing the initial prescription. All requests must be recorded on the patient's chart, including the name of the pharmacist involved and the purpose of the request. No claim may be made for telephone calls in which only a physician proxy, (e.g., nurse or clerk) speaks with the pharmacist. No claim may be made when a physician directs a patient to request the pharmacist to call, fax or e-mail a renewal request. Where the pharmacist requests a prescription renewal by facsimile, the physician may respond by telephone or facsimile, and submit a claim for this request. This code is not intended to cover calls made to clarify a prescription or decipher an illegible prescription, switching to a generic form of a drug or requesting EDS, these services are part of the visit service that involved the writing of the initial prescription. No claim may be made for telephone calls regarding patients in a hospital receiving acute care. Not payable in addition to another service on the same day for the same patient by same practitioner.

The Mental Health Planning Fee requires a face-to-face visit with the patient and/or the patient’s medical representative. Identifies an appropriate time frame for follow up and re-evaluation of the patient’s progress and Mental Health Plan. Provides confirmation that the Mental Health Plan has been communicated verbally or in writing to the patient and/or the patient’s Medical Representative, and to other involved allied care professionals as appropriate. Payable once per fiscal year per patient. Not intended as a routine annual fee unless the severity of the illness requires a comprehensive Mental Health Plan review and revision.
